[model-reply-parse-fails-open-loudly] Rule · A step that reads a model's reply must find the result anywhere in it, and say so on the PR when there is none
symptom: a CI step that reviews a PR with a model reports 'could not parse the reply', passes, and the PR merges with no review verdict
fix: extract the last JSON object carrying the expected keys from anywhere in the reply; when none is found, still fail open if blocking would train bypass, but annotate the PR (::warning) that there is no verdict; test with a prose-prefixed reply, stray braces, a reply quoting the format, and none

[merge-needs-resolved-threads] Rule · main requires resolved review conversations — a green PR stays BLOCKED until bot threads are resolved
symptom: every check on a PR passes, gh pr merge says the requirements are not met (mergeStateStatus BLOCKED), and a merge-and-wait loop stalls
fix: after addressing a review finding, reply on the thread with the fixing commit and resolve it (gh api graphql resolveReviewThread with the thread id from reviewThreads), then merge; check mergeStateStatus before assuming a check is pending

[seed:dotnet-canon:r_encoding_loop] Rule · Encode every 'never again / always when' finding to the smallest surface that catches it — a fix PR without the rule is a half-finished job
symptom: a merged fix for a recurring antipattern with no corresponding rule/gate change
fix: land the rule with the fix (same or paired PR); track deferred encodings as labeled placeholders, never as the encoding itself

[n_a7634ef53a8f] Decision · The encoding loop has no runtime input — every lesson enters from author time or CI time
symptom: a defect class that only a running system reveals (pagination silently dropped, a limit hit under real load, a partial-failure path) has no way into the store until a human finds it some other way
fix: treat observability as a SOURCE of records rather than a competitor to them: when a runtime-only defect is found, record it with found_by naming the trace or metric that showed it; do not claim the loop covers runtime until some record actually cites one

[n_e99ea322dee5] Defect · A review bot that skips a PR reports success — a green check is not a review
symptom: a PR shows the review bot's check green and has no review comments, and nobody asked whether a review ran
fix: read the check's description, not its colour; count the bot's actual reviews and comments; on a repo where the bot reviews on request only, request it explicitly ('@coderabbitai review') and wait before merging

[n_ce6a27cc432f] Defect · A resolver that falls back to a default location turns a missing setup into a successful write nobody reads
symptom: a write command run before setup, or in the wrong directory, exits 0, and the data never appears where every reader looks
fix: make the resolver refuse when nothing names the target (one exception the entry point turns into 'could not run'), instead of guarding commands one at a time; test that every command exits 2, prints nothing to stdout, and leaves no file behind

[optional-feature-shipped-text] Defect · Making a feature optional leaves every shipped sentence that assumes it false somewhere
symptom: a reviewer in a consumer repo flags generated text describing a gate, step or file that repo was set up without
fix: when a feature becomes optional, grep every shipped template for sentences that assume it and reword them to what holds in every configuration (here: the briefing and okl drift mark the lesson STALE; a gate fails where installed). Fix generated files upstream in the template, never in the consumer repo.

[n_8519bf0f71c6] Gate · The encoding loop's write side needs a mechanical catch — a session-end hook that asks 'what did we learn?'
symptom: sessions end with fixed code but no recorded lesson; the same finding resurfaces in a later review
fix: install stop-okl-encode.sh (okl init or okl scaffold) and register it under hooks.Stop

[review-bot-watch-matches-wrong-comment] Defect · A wait loop keyed on a review bot's result text matched the same words inside a skip or rate-limit notice, and missed a finding added by an edit
symptom: a background watch reports a review as finished or clean, but the PR has no new review; or a finding appears in a comment that was already read
fix: key the wait on a review object (pulls/<n>/reviews with a body) or on the reply to YOUR request, created after it, never on the bot's status check, which reads 'pass' when it hit its review limit and reviewed nothing (quartzose #14, emeraldleaf-dev #28, 2026-10-10); reject any comment carrying the bot's rate-limit or skip marker; a 'Review finished' reply is not a review either, since the bot is incremental and answers a request with it while skipping commits it already saw (quartzose #18, 2026-10-24): require a review object or a 'No actionable comments' note updated after the last push; after each review, list the bot's comments by updated_at as well as created_at, and re-read any edited after you replied; and read the review's body, not only its inline comments: a finding on lines outside the PR's diff cannot be posted inline, so it appears only in the body under 'Outside diff range comments', with no inline comment and no 'Actionable comments posted' line (okl #280, 2026-10-24). A clean note counts only when its 'Reviewing files ... between X and Y' line ends at the PR's head and the summary is not marked 'Currently processing': while a new review runs, the summary keeps the previous review's 'No actionable comments' line beside the in-progress marker, so it read as clean two minutes into a full review (okl #286, 2026-10-25). And an empty-bodied review object is the container for the bot's reply on a thread, not a review, yet it marks the head reviewed: a plain request then answers 'Action not completed', and only '@coderabbitai full review' reviews the changes since (okl #286, 2026-10-25)

[n_b550ba9c5c8a] Rule · Diagrams and the README are review surfaces — held by a claims gate, not by drift enrolment
symptom: a diagram or README states counts, figures or components the report or code no longer supports; or a committed diagram nothing links to
fix: edit the .excalidraw source and re-render (the SVG is a render; say loudly in the commit if it is stale); run ./ci/check-diagram-figures.sh; delete a diagram nothing links to rather than maintain it

[thesis-maintain-anything] Decision · okl's scope is everything a team maintains: keep the agent true to your rules, specs and docs, keep those current as the code moves, and keep learning
symptom: work on okl that treats it as a store of lessons only, or treats docs, diagrams, specs, the report, results or research as outside its job; or a change to what okl is for that leaves the thesis and its measured baseline as they were
fix: hold okl's work to this scope (issue #317): anything a team maintains can be tied to what it describes, flagged when that moves, brought back in line by the agent in the session with the person told or asked first, and confirmed by a check or an honest review; keep detection mechanical (no model calls in okl's own loop) and write nothing to the store without the person knowing; keep docs/THESIS.md and its baseline current whenever the thesis or the measured results move The thesis (docs/THESIS.md) is the primary, complete record of that scope: every promise okl makes today, in the README, the docs or the maintainer's site, is listed there with its status and evidence, and a wider direction is added beside those promises, never in place of them; when other copy promises something the thesis does not, update the thesis deliberately or correct the copy.

[generated-diagram-traced-old-path] Defect · A generated diagram went wrong anyway: its generator traced a code path production had stopped using, and its freshness test only compared it with its own render
symptom: a diagram generated from the code shows counts the live system no longer produces, while its freshness test stays green
fix: make the generator call the functions production calls, not a re-implementation of them, and cross-check its result against the production entry point (here _live_hits) so it aborts when they disagree; a render-vs-generator freshness test cannot notice the generator drifting from production

[n_5ddb0776a863] Defect · A CI gate that reads gitignored state checks nothing in CI, and passes
symptom: a gate is green on every PR and never red, and the data it inspects lives in a file the repository ignores
fix: make the gate count what it inspected and treat zero as 'did not run' (its own exit code), never as clean; then decide explicitly how CI gets the data, rather than letting its absence read as success. The same holds for any report or summary line that states a clean result: carry the inspected count beside it and say 'unknown' at zero (okl recap --report printed 'every lesson is proven' with drift having checked nothing, caught in review on okl #281, 2026-10-24)

[worktree-no-store-reverify] Rule · A git worktree has no okl store: re-verify drift from the main checkout after moving the branch there
symptom: a branch built in a git worktree (a workflow's isolation: worktree, or git worktree add) changes files that rules govern, and okl verify / okl reverify cannot run there, so the PR's drift gate would go red
fix: commit and push the branch from the worktree, then git worktree remove it (a branch checked out in a worktree cannot be switched to elsewhere), git switch to the branch in the main checkout, run okl reverify --yes, commit okl-drift.json, and confirm okl drift --gate --snapshot okl-drift.json exits 0 after that commit, since the gate reads the committed snapshot. Do not point OKL_DATABASE_URL at the main store from the worktree without its config: the store takes the folder name as the repo, skips repo-scoped rules and looks like it worked; if you must verify there, copy .okl/config.json in first

[empty-drift-snapshot-fails-ci] Defect · A committed drift snapshot with zero rules fails CI, and okl verify never creates the first one
symptom: a new user commits okl-drift.json on day one, before any lesson has --files, and the okl-verify CI step fails with 'NOTHING CHECKED' (exit 2); or a user verifies a lesson and finds no okl-drift.json to commit
fix: commit okl-drift.json only once a lesson governs files: run okl export --drift once, then let okl verify refresh it; documented in the Quickstart. Candidate code fix: have export --drift refuse (exit 2) to write a snapshot with zero rules, so the trap cannot be set

symptom: a topology/pattern-changing PR with no doc or diagram delta
fix: update the depicting doc/diagram in the same PR, or name the deferred issue in the PR body

[n_6b65aa35593c] Rule · A diagram with numbers in it is generated from the system, or it is already wrong
symptom: a committed diagram or doc states counts, thresholds or shapes that someone transcribed by hand
fix: generate the artifact from the live system and add a freshness test that regenerates and diffs; trace against committed inputs, never a developer's local state, or the test passes only on the machine that last rendered it

symptom: a docs or README table of measured figures quotes numbers its cited receipts do not contain, or its columns come from runs at different commits or store sizes, so a difference between columns may be the store and not the setting
fix: re-run every column in one sitting at one commit against one store, print the table from those receipts with a script (okl: evals/standing_table.py), and have the script refuse receipts that disagree on commit or store size; label configurations that differ in more than the setting under comparison (okl: harness versus hook interests)

fix: no run, no stamp: verification API takes evidence produced by an executed check; keep assertion-based flags only for importing historical receipts

fix: keep the shipped set as a FLOOR and let the store declare additions as records; validate against floor union declared, and validate the declaration itself against the floor only so the first one is writable

symptom: a step or safeguard deleted on the strength of 'the code already does this', with no test asserting it
fix: write the test that makes the claim executable BEFORE deleting the thing that compensated for it; prove it by breaking the behaviour and watching the test go red

[n_713b8c104f12] Defect · An empty result and a mistyped filter must not look identical
symptom: a query with a filter flag returns zero rows and exit 0, and the flag value was never validated
fix: validate the filter's FORM and refuse a malformed one with exit 2; for a well-formed value the data has never seen, still run but say so and name the values that do exist

symptom: an installer prints manual follow-up steps (register this hook, copy this workflow, add to settings)
fix: make init perform each registration itself, idempotent and non-clobbering; warn loudly only for what it truly cannot do (e.g. no git repo -> drift disabled)

symptom: a documented storage env var works in one entry point and is silently overridden in another; writes land somewhere other than where the operator pointed them
fix: resolve the storage target in ONE place that every entry point calls; if a component deliberately ignores the variable, refuse loudly rather than silently substituting a default

symptom: after renaming a package, service, or identifier, a conditional that greps for the old name stops matching and takes its fallback branch without erroring
fix: grep the old name to zero across CI, scripts, and docs as part of the rename; key capability checks on structure (a path that must exist) rather than on a name that can change

symptom: after a refactor moves or renames a module, a repo's own CI starts testing the released package instead of the branch, and every check stays green
fix: detect a checkout by its package root (src/okl/__init__.py), not by one module; before moving or renaming a file, grep every workflow, script and test for its old path (the rename rule)

symptom: okl init --dry-run, re-run in a repo whose .okl/config.json says repo=quartzose, announces 'okl init --repo Quartzose'; running it would rewrite the repo name
fix: fixed in 1b97b0a (2026-10-05): init takes --repo, else the name in this directory's own .okl/config.json, else the folder's name, so a plain re-run keeps the configured name. tests/test_okl.py::test_init_rerun_keeps_the_configured_repo_name guards it; if a re-run or its dry run proposes a different repo name again, that guard has regressed

fix: Before acting on what an owned file does, read the copy on disk, scoped to the part that matters and ignoring comments (install._workflow_reads_pin); when it lacks the behaviour, act on nothing, say so, and name okl init --force

fix: pass log=False to Client.check (okl intake does; the service honours it as the check request's log field), or set OKL_BRIEFING_LOG=0 before building the Client in an eval or pre-flight script; test it by running the caller against a throwaway store and asserting no briefing row was written

symptom: a specific task's briefing lists 80%+ of all nodes in scope as relevant
fix: add a relevance cutoff (rank score threshold or top-k) so the briefing stays short; measure against the ADR's miss-rate trigger before tightening

[n_9ba48d85ed19] Gate · Pre-flight the retrieval before spending on an eval — it is deterministic and answers in milliseconds
symptom: an eval result read as a regression, with no check that each case still receives the input it is testing
fix: run a pre-flight asserting every case's governing record is present in the retrieval it will be given; refuse the run on an unexpected miss; keep known gaps in a named register with reasons, never silent

symptom: someone proposes backfilling applies_to across the whole corpus, or asks whether the field is pulling its weight
fix: keep it unset by default and set it only per-record at record time; re-measure the two shares before changing the policy, and never derive the value from a tag
